question.text: In the context of investment adviser services, 'financial advisory' differs from 'execution' in that:

answer.text: Advisory involves research while execution involves sales only
Advisory involves providing advice or recommendation for consideration, while execution involves carrying out or implementing the investment transactions
Advisory is regulated by SEBI while execution is regulated by RBI
Advisory is free of charge while execution involves fees

explanation.text: The Logic: Financial advisory means providing advice or recommendation for consideration, while execution or implementation involves actually carrying out the transactions arising from that advice. Fee-only advisers typically refer execution elsewhere. The Trap: Saying execution is RBI-regulated instead of SEBI-regulated is wrong as worded; execution-only services may involve products regulated by multiple regulators, so labelling both functions as solely SEBI-regulated would also overstate the source. Note: Investment Advisers may provide implementation services only through direct schemes/products and without receiving any consideration for the implementation.
